reason: For the given input both partial writes target the same set of the same bank and the second one arrives while the first is still pending and not the entry chosen by the drain (forward: an older lower-index entry S' is ahead in PriorityEncoder order; reverse: the bank read port stalls the drain). Because the ITTAGE write request carries no tag and the write buffer resolves a pending-entry hit by wholesale replacement of entry, setIdx and bitmask (WriteBuffer.scala:175-177) rather than by merging disjoint bitmasks, the earlier partial write (all-but-useful in forward order, useful-only in reverse order) is silently dropped. The required result (SRAM set S ends with D1's tag/cnt/target and usefulCnt=0) is not produced: forward order yields usefulCnt=0 only with stale tag/cnt/target, reverse order yields D1's fields with usefulCnt unchanged. This violates R-ITTAGE-6 on the 'must not silently discard another decided write' half; the 'must not change unintended fields' half is not itself violated because the surviving write still carries its own correct bitmask.
